subject.title: Unhandled Playwright assertion error in CRSession._onMessage crashes Gateway

question: Should OpenClaw address this CRSession assertion with a narrow browser-owned recovery path after live repro, or should the work wait for a broader browser/CDP subprocess isolation design?
rationale: The source path is plausible, but the permanent fix changes the Gateway crash boundary and reconnect semantics, so automation should not choose between targeted suppression and process isolation without maintainer intent.

options.title: Require live repro, then add browser-owned recovery
options.body: Capture the CRSession CDP message path first, then implement the narrowest handler that logs, tears down or reconnects the affected Playwright connection, and keeps the Gateway alive.

options.title: Design subprocess isolation first
options.body: Pause code repair until maintainers define a browser worker or child-process boundary that can crash independently from the Gateway.

options.title: Defer until another production repro
options.body: Keep the issue open but avoid implementation until a current-main log identifies the exact CDP message shape.

recommendation.title: Require live repro, then add browser-owned recovery
recommendation.body: Capture the CRSession CDP message path first, then implement the narrowest handler that logs, tears down or reconnects the affected Playwright connection, and keeps the Gateway alive.

likelyOwner.reason: He is tied to both the browser plugin ownership change and the global unhandled-rejection setup, so he is the best available owner for the crash-boundary choice.
